audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers tell opposite stories: full says HARD 8/10 with Yasuo winning all seven stages; content and the packet levelChart give Mel all seven. Win rate 48.46% supports neither extreme.
audit.why: I cannot adjudicate seven rows from the kits alone, so per the chart rule I left every row untouched and flagged the whole chart for the user.
audit.corrected: None to the chart; the false mechanism the content chart leaned on is fixed (see point 4).

audit.why: Spikes: his level 2 (two abilities + flow shield), tornado at Q stacks, Last Breath at 6 (70s CD rank 1), Mel Luden's window. Content spike texts cover these once the wall claim is fixed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer's central claim — 'Solar Snare (E) is a ground root that ignores Wind Wall' — contradicts the kit: Mel's E is flagged projectile ('can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects') and Riot's text says she FIRES a radiant orb forward. It repeats in whys[2], whys[5], whys[6], spikes[0], spikes[2], spikes[3], mid, late and wants.you[0].
audit.why: Both Mel Q and Mel E are wall-blockable. The true edge is uptime: Wind Wall blocks for 4s on a 25s cooldown while her E is back every 11s and Q every 10s — plus Rebuttal reflecting the tornado denies his Last Breath setup entirely.
audit.corrected: Every 'ignores/through the wall' claim rewritten to the cooldown-uptime mechanism at the same length.

audit.why: Trade shape (poke max range, commit only with wall down, punish post-shield) is right.
Wind Wall 25/23/21/19/17s, 4s duration; Last Breath 70/50/30s; Mel W 38s, E 11s.
Wave guidance is serviceable; freezing against a waveclear-poor melee is fine.
Roam/jungle text is Mel-specific and sound.
Zhonya's already recommended for divers — apt here.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your Q, chaining Sweeping Blade through the wave, and cashing a tornado into Last Breath on you.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Rebuttal like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Yasuo Wind Wall: 25s at rank 1, blocks projectiles for 4s — hold Q and E until it's spent; your E is back every 11s, his wall isn't. - Last Breath is 70s at rank 1: reflect the tornado and it never comes. - Guard your 38s Rebuttal for the all-in.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks mean a tornado is loaded — casting Q rooted in place invites the knockup into Last Breath; move between volleys.

notes: Killed the page's central false mechanic: Mel's Solar Snare is a fired projectile (kit flag: wall-blockable), not a ground-targeted cast, so 'ignores Wind Wall' was wrong in nine places — all rewritten to the true edge (4s wall on 25s CD vs her 11s E / 10s Q uptime, plus Rebuttal reflecting the tornado to deny Last Breath setup). Left the entire level chart untouched: full says Yasuo 7/7 (HARD 8/10), content+packet say Mel 7/7, WR is 48.46%; both extremes look wrong and the kits alone cannot settle each row — question raised for the user rather than guessed.
